query-load-series.read: Request rate, queue depth or consumer lag for the workload, against the kill times.

query-memory-series.read: container_memory_working_set_bytes for the container over the incident window.

read-config-audit.read: Who changed which ConfigMap or Secret, and when.

read-container-spec.read: Resources, probes, and the command, args and env the runtime starts with.

read-container-state.limits: `ran_for` is the last terminated instance's lifetime only; a trend across many lifetimes is not visible here.
read-container-state.read: Each container's last terminated state: exit code, and `ran_for` -- how long that one instance lived, which is not how often the container restarts. get_pod_container_statuses gives the same for one pod.

read-events.read: Kill, back-off and probe events for the workload's pods: a count over the span from first_seen to last_seen gives the restart interval, which is not an instance's lifetime. Compare across replicas.

read-previous-logs.read: The previous instance's logs (previous=true): how it ended, and whether it got as far as serving.

read-rollout-history.limits: ConfigMap and Secret *edits* leave no ReplicaSet revision, so "the workload spec is unchanged" does not establish that the configuration is unchanged.
read-rollout-history.read: When the workload's spec, image and limits last changed, against the onset.

sample-memory-now.limits: One sample, taken now. It can show usage near the limit; it cannot show growth within a life, a peak, or anything before the sample.

application-crash.note: Exit 137 with nothing logged before the cut means the process was killed from outside rather than failing on its own.
application-crash.title: application crash

bad-config.note: Where the configuration history cannot be seen, say so rather than treating an unchanged workload as ruling this out.
bad-config.title: bad config

failed-liveness-probe.note: Terminated with SIGTERM (143) rather than SIGKILL. No probe configured on the container at all rules this out outright, rather than merely weakening it.
failed-liveness-probe.title: failed liveness probe

memory-leak.note: Killed before it finishes starting means there was no period of operation in which anything could accumulate. Without a memory time series this can be weakened or refuted on timing alone but not confirmed, and an answer that states a peak usage figure has invented it.
memory-leak.title: memory leak

memory-limit-too-low.note: The limit is small relative to what the runtime needs by default -- a JVM, Go or Node process with no heap or arena sizing flags set sizes itself from the cgroup, so a limit equal to the request and no such flags is the shape to look for. When it is refuted, something about the workload changed, not the provisioning.
memory-limit-too-low.title: memory limit too low

oom-kill.note: The process was killed from outside (SIGKILL), not failing on its own.
oom-kill.title: OOM

workload-spike.note: A container that never reaches readiness served no traffic at all, so no request can have driven its memory up.
workload-spike.title: workload spike

completes_startup_each_life.says: the container completes startup and serves for a while in each life (it reaches readiness)

config_change_precedes_first_failure.says: a ConfigMap, Secret or environment change precedes the first failure

exits_before_listener.says: the process exits before opening its listener

healthy_on_same_config.says: the workload has been unchanged for a long period and ran healthily on this same configuration before the failures began

healthy_period_before_kills.says: the container ran healthily for a long period on this same limit before the kills began

killed_on_every_life.says: the container is killed on every restart including the first, with no period of healthy operation that grew shorter over time

kills_evenly_spaced_under_flat_load.says: the kills are evenly spaced through a period of flat or absent load

last_exit_code.says: the container's last termination exit code is {Code}

lifetime_steady_or_shortening.says: instance lifetime (how long each instance runs before it is killed) is roughly constant or shortening across many restarts

lifetime_varies_without_trend.says: instance lifetime varies widely with no trend across restarts

limit_equals_request.says: the container's {Resource} limit equals its request

limit_or_image_changed_before_onset.says: the memory limit or the image changed before the kills began

liveness_probe_configured.says: a liveness probe is configured on the container

load_rise_coincides_with_kills.says: kills coincide with a rise in request rate, queue depth or consumer lag

logs_name_invalid_setting.says: the logs name a missing or invalid setting

memory_grows_within_life.says: memory climbs monotonically within each life rather than spiking

memory_limit_plausibly_reached.says: the memory limit is one the workload plausibly reaches

peers_share_kill_timing.says: peers handling the same traffic show the same kill timing

probe_failures_before_restarts.says: events show Unhealthy or probe-failure entries immediately before each restart

process_logged_fatal_error.says: the process's own logs end with an exception, stack trace or fatal error before the cut

restarts_before_initial_delay.says: restarts happen sooner than the probe's initialDelaySeconds

runtime_sizing_flags_set.says: heap or arena sizing flags are set for the runtime

note: Built by k8srca.kb.build. 'related' is the bidirectional correlation graph from correlated_alerts. 'group' is a coarse label, not a causal parent. 'knowledge' is the authored layer (design 007); an alert it maps to a symptom is answered from there.
